full_judgment:
14. Mr Fazlul Haq Khan Farid, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the appellants in Criminal Appeal No. 1797 of 2003, adopts the submissions made by learned Advocate Mr Khandker Mahbub Hossain. He further submits that the delay in lodging the first information report gave the informant an opportunity to concoct the story and implicate all the accused persons who are inimical to her. He points out that, according to the evidence of witnesses, the police station is only half a mile away from the hospital and she need not have waited for two days before lodging the first information report, especially when the police apparently went to the place of occurrence on the very night of occurrence and seized alamats. He refers to the seizure list which was prepared by the police at 9-30 PM on 23-8-99 on the basis of GD Entry No. 978 dated 23-8-99. Referring to the evidence of witnesses, he highlights the number of cases in which the two parties were involved either as informant, accused or witnesses, which is a fact admitted by the witnesses in cross-examination. He submits that in the light of such evidence of admitted enmity between the parties, the evidence of prosecution witnesses must be considered very cautiously. He submits that the evidence of PWs 2, 3, 4, 13 and 14 indicate that the prosecution story was concocted subsequently, particularly since PWs 13 and 14, who saw the appellants at that scene of the first place of occurrence, failed to name any of them. Pointing to the explanation given by the informant for the delay in lodging the first information report, the learned Advocate submits that if, as she says, she lodged the first information report after her husband regained consciousness, then it follows that he was not conscious until 25-8-99, which falsifies the dying declaration allegedly recorded on 23-8-99. With regard to appellant Razzak Mia, the learned Advocate points out that it is apparent from a glance at the first information report form and the written first information report filed by the informant that the name of accused No. 14 Razzak was inserted subsequently. He points out that the insertion in the form is obvious and the interpolation in the body of the first information report is apparent to the naked eye and, as such, he submits, the complicity of appellant Abdur Razzak Mia is an afterthought and his complicity in the alleged occurrence is highly doubtful. He also points out that attention of the investigating officer (PW 16) was drawn to this fact and he admitted the overwriting in the first information report. He prays for acquittal of the appellants, whom he represents. 

 49. On careful assessment of the evidence of the witnesses, we find that, first of all, the first information report did not at the outset contain the name under serial No. 14 of accused Razzak Mia; we find that serial No. 14 has been inserted in such a way in the first information report form that it is apparent on the face of the record that the number and name were inserted subsequently. Also a close scrutiny of the body of the first information report indicates to the naked eye that there was interpolation and that the name of this accused had been inserted subsequently. Accordingly, we are in no doubt that there was interpolation of the record at some stage, which has led to inclusion of the name of accused Abdur Razzak alias Abdur Razzak Mia and such doubt can only go to the benefit of the accused and he must, therefore, be acquitted of the charge leveled against him.
